user: The Yoneda lemma is a powerful tool in category theory that states that an object in a category can be uniquely determined by how other objects in the category relate to it via morphisms. In the context of cobordisms, which involve topological spaces and manifolds, the Yoneda lemma can be used to study these spaces and manifolds by focusing on how other objects (in this case, cobordisms) relate to them through the lens of representable functors and essential isomorphisms.
